name: Snake
intro: A snake is a reptile with a long body and no legs. There are thousands of kinds of snakes.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A snake is a reptile.
It has a long body and no legs.
Its body is covered with scales.
A snake has no eyelids, so it cannot blink.
Some snakes are shorter than a pencil.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Snakes live on every continent but Antarctica.
They live in forests, swamps, grasslands, and deserts.
Some snakes live in water, even in the ocean.
Most snakes live in warm places.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: All snakes eat other animals.
They eat mice, fish, frogs, and eggs.
Snakes cannot chew.
They swallow their food whole.
After a big meal, a snake may not eat for weeks.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: Many baby snakes hatch from eggs.
Some baby snakes are born alive.
Most baby snakes take care of themselves.
Snakes keep growing their whole lives.
They shed their old skin as they grow.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A snake flicks its tongue to smell the air.
Snakes move by squeezing their muscles.
Some tree snakes can glide from tree to tree.
Sea snakes use their flat tails like paddles.
Most snakes are not dangerous to people.

vocab.meaning: An animal with scaly skin, like a snake or turtle.
Small, hard pieces that cover an animal's skin.
To lose old skin so new skin can show.
An animal that eats other animals.
